question: In a common rail diesel injection system, what is the primary function of the pressure limiting valve?
options: A. To regulate fuel pressure to the injectors during normal operation
B. To protect the high-pressure pump and rail from overpressure by diverting fuel back to the tank
C. To control the quantity of fuel injected per cycle
D. To maintain a minimum pressure in the low-pressure circuit

question: During a cylinder contribution test on a diesel engine using a diagnostic scan tool, one cylinder shows a significantly higher fuel quantity correction than others. What does this most likely indicate?
options: A. The injector in that cylinder is delivering too much fuel
B. The injector in that cylinder has high mechanical wear and requires more fuel to maintain idle speed
C. The fuel pressure regulator is faulty
D. The turbocharger is over-boosting on that cylinder bank

question: A vehicle fitted with a Variable Geometry Turbocharger (VGT) exhibits black smoke under load and low boost pressure. The wastegate actuator has been confirmed as functional. What is the most likely cause?
options: A. Sticking or seized variable vanes due to carbon buildup
B. A faulty mass airflow sensor
C. Excessive engine oil consumption causing fouled injectors
D. A blocked diesel particulate filter

question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of pilot injection in a common rail diesel system?
options: A. To cool the combustion chamber before main injection
B. To reduce combustion noise by pre-igniting a small fuel quantity before the main injection event
C. To lubricate the injector needle
D. To purge air from the high-pressure circuit

question: In an automotive air conditioning system, a technician measures suction pressure of 350 kPa and discharge pressure of 1100 kPa with the system running. The ambient temperature is 30°C. What condition does this most likely indicate?
options: A. Normal operating condition
B. Refrigerant overcharge or condenser airflow restriction
C. Refrigerant undercharge
D. Expansion valve stuck open

question: A vehicle with an electronically controlled automatic transmission exhibits harsh upshifts only at wide-open throttle. All shift solenoids test within specification. What is the most likely cause?
options: A. Low transmission fluid level
B. A faulty throttle position sensor providing incorrect load data to the TCM
C. A worn torque converter clutch
D. Incorrect transmission fluid type

question: When performing a four-wheel alignment, a technician notices that the rear axle thrust angle is 0.5° to the left. What effect will this have on the vehicle's handling?
options: A. The vehicle will pull to the right during braking
B. The front wheels must be steered slightly right to track straight, causing the steering wheel to be off-centre
C. The vehicle will oversteer during cornering
D. There will be excessive tyre wear on the front left tyre only

question: A vehicle's ABS activates during normal braking on dry pavement at speeds below 30 km/h. Scan tool data shows wheel speed sensor signals are consistent. What is the most likely cause?
options: A. A faulty ABS control module
B. Excessive lateral runout on a brake rotor causing a false wheel deceleration signal
C. Low brake fluid level
D. Worn brake pads triggering the ABS prematurely

question: In an electronically controlled power steering system (EPS), what parameter does the ECU primarily use to determine the level of steering assistance required?
options: A. Vehicle speed and torque sensor input from the steering column
B. Engine load and coolant temperature
C. Lateral acceleration from the yaw rate sensor
D. Throttle position and battery voltage

question: A technician is testing a piezoelectric fuel injector on a common rail system. The oscilloscope waveform shows a characteristic voltage spike during the closing phase. What does this spike indicate?
options: A. A short circuit in the injector winding
B. The piezoelectric stack recovering energy as it contracts, which is normal operation
C. Fuel pressure in the rail is too high
D. The injector driver circuit in the ECU is failing

question: When diagnosing an engine misfire using a pressure transducer in the combustion chamber, a low and late pressure rise on one cylinder compared to others would most likely indicate which condition?
options: A. A leaking exhaust valve
B. An intake manifold vacuum leak on that cylinder
C. Retarded ignition timing on that cylinder or a weak injector pulse
D. A cracked piston crown

question: A hybrid electric vehicle's high-voltage battery management system (BMS) triggers a fault isolating the battery from the drive system. Which of the following conditions would most likely cause this response?
options: A. A detected ground fault (isolation fault) between the high-voltage circuit and the vehicle chassis
B. Low 12V auxiliary battery voltage
C. Regenerative braking system overload
D. Coolant temperature sensor failure in the low-voltage circuit

question: During a relative compression test using a current clamp on the battery cable, a technician observes that one cylinder shows a noticeably lower current draw during cranking. What does this indicate?
options: A. That cylinder has the highest compression
B. That cylinder has lower compression, requiring less starter motor effort to crank through
C. There is excessive friction on that cylinder's piston rings
D. The fuel injector for that cylinder is stuck open

question: An engine management system uses a wideband (broadband) lambda sensor rather than a narrowband sensor. What is the primary operational advantage of the wideband sensor in engine management?
options: A. It provides a precise rich/lean switching signal for faster closed-loop response
B. It generates a linear output voltage across a wide range of air-fuel ratios, enabling accurate fuelling control under all operating conditions
C. It is immune to exhaust back pressure variations
D. It eliminates the need for a catalytic converter monitoring sensor downstream

question: A technician performing a charged cooling system pressure test notices the pressure drops steadily but there are no visible external leaks, and combustion gas tests are negative. What is the most likely cause of the pressure loss?
options: A. A faulty radiator pressure cap
B. An internal leak within the heater core
C. A cracked engine block internally routing coolant to the crankcase
D. A leaking coolant reservoir tank
